ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.claim: The concluding discourse returns to the sūrah's opening theme: Qur'anic warnings are true, punishment signs can come, and prophetic histories already serve as signs for the stubborn Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.anchor: Coming up are the concluding verses of the sūrah and the discourse links to its introductory part which is the real theme.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r4.claim: The majority read taqallub as a verbal noun coordinated with the object in God seeing the Prophet; Janah ibn Hubaysh reads it as a present verb coordinated with يراك.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وتقلبك مصدر تقلب، وعطف على الكاف في يراك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r5.claim: Mujahid and Qatada gloss those prostrating as people who pray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: في الساجدين: في المصلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's light passed through the loins of Adam, Noah, and Abraham until his emergence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في أصلاب آدم ونوح وإبراهيم حتى خرجت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r7.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r7.claim: Ikrima understands God to see the Prophet standing and prostrating.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r9.claim: Mujahid also says the Prophet's turning is his looking among those praying behind him, as in a report that he saw worshippers behind his back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r9.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: المراد تقلب بصره فيمن يصلي خلفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says prayer is the apparent sense, though Mujahid and Qatada allow all the Prophet's activities and movements among worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.anchor: ظاهر الآية أنه يريد قيام الصلاة، ويحتمل أن يريد سائر التصرفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and others take the prostrators as those praying with the Prophet; Ibn Abbas and Qatada also mean believers generally, described as prostrators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r11.anchor: أي صلاتك مع المصلين، قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة وغيرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r12.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r12.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the phrase means the Prophet's movement among the prophets, like their movements.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r12.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: أراد الأنبياء، أي تقلبك كما تقلب غيرك من الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari pictures the Prophet praying at night and discreetly checking his companions' worship and inner states; after night prayer was abrogated, he toured their homes and heard their devotional murmuring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.anchor: طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون، بحرصه عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r1.claim: The prostrators can mean worshippers, and the verse may describe God seeing the Prophet lead congregational prayer through standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r1.anchor: والمراد بالساجدين: المصلون. وقيل: معناه يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r2.claim: Maqatil reports asking Abu Hanifa whether congregational prayer appears in the Quran; Abu Hanifa cited this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r2.anchor: وعن مقاتل، أنه سأل أبا حنيفة رضي الله عنه: هل تجد الصلاة في الجماعة في القرآن؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r3.claim: The phrase may also assure that no aspect of the Prophet's state is hidden when he rises and moves among worshippers while managing religious affairs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا يخفى علي حالك كلما قمت وتقلبت مع الساجدين في كفاية أمور الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r5.speaker: الرافضة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r5.claim: The Rafidites argue that the Prophet's forefathers were believers, construing the verse as God transferring his spirit from one prostrator to another; they say all possible senses should be retained because none conflicts or prevails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r5.anchor: وذهبت الرافضة إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r6.speaker: الرافضة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r6.claim: They also cite a prophetic report that the Prophet was passed through pure loins and wombs, and infer that disbelievers are impure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p198/r6.anchor: لم أزل أنقل من أصلاب الطاهرين إلى أرحام الطاهرات

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.claim: One interpretation is the Prophet’s night worship and his movement among the worshippers; “those prostrating” means the worshippers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.anchor: المراد ما كان يفعله في جوف الليل من قيامه للتهجد

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.claim: An anonymous report says that after the night vigil ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet visited his Companions’ homes that night to see their worship, hearing them hum with remembrance like wasps in their nests; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.anchor: كما يحكى أنه حين نسخ فرض قيام الليل طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.claim: A second interpretation is that the Prophet rises to lead the congregation and moves among the worshippers in standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.anchor: المعنى يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة وتقلبه في الساجدين تصرفه فيما بينهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.claim: A third interpretation is that God never misses the Prophet’s state whenever he rises or moves among the worshippers while managing religious affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.anchor: أنه لا يخفى عليه حالك كلما قمت وتقلبت مع الساجدين في كفاية أمور الدين

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r9.claim: A fourth interpretation takes the Prophet’s “movement” as his gaze moving among those behind him, since he said that he saw them from behind while they prayed.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r9.anchor: المراد تقلب بصره فيمن ( يلي ) خلفه

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r10.claim: Rāzī cites Muhammad’s statement, “Complete bowing and prostration; by God, I see you from behind”; he gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r10.anchor: من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أتموا الركوع والسجود فوالله إني لأراكم من خلفي )

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r11.claim: “The All-Hearing” concerns what the Prophet says; “the All-Knowing” concerns what he intends and does.

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r12.claim: Hearing is a distinct divine attribute from knowledge of things heard; otherwise “All-Knowing” would add nothing to “All-Hearing.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r12.anchor: كونه سميعا أمر مغاير لعلمه بالمسموعات

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r13.claim: Rāzī notes a reading with the first-person plural verb “وَنُقَلِّبُكَ”.

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.claim: The Rāfiḍa argue that the Prophet’s ancestors were believers and take the verse to allow God to have transferred his soul from one prostrating ancestor to another.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.claim: The Rāfiḍa also cite the report that the Prophet was continually transferred from pure loins to pure wombs, reasoning that every unbeliever is impure; the verse is in 9:28. Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( لم أزل أنقل من أصلاب الطاهرين إلى أرحام الطاهرات )

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.claim: To answer the reference to Abraham’s father Āzar, they say “father” can mean uncle: Jacob’s sons call Ishmael their father though he was their uncle, and the Prophet called al-ʿAbbās “my father.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.claim: They also allow “father” to mean a maternal grandfather, citing Jesus’ inclusion among Abraham’s descendants although Abraham was his maternal grandfather.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.claim: Rāzī holds to the apparent sense of “his father Āzar”; the Rāfiḍa’s explanation shifts the word away from its apparent meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.anchor: بقوله تعالى : { لابيه ءازر } وما ذكروه صرف للفظ عن ظاهره

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.claim: Rāzī rejects taking the shared expression in all its possible senses at once, since an ambiguous word cannot carry all of them together.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.anchor: لما بينا أن حمل المشترك على كل معانيه غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.claim: The report about pure loins and wombs is a solitary report and therefore cannot outweigh the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.anchor: وأما الحديث فهو خبر واحد فلا يعارض القرآن

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r1.claim: Taqallub means turning about; here it refers to the Prophet’s rounds to inspect the states of night worshippers.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r1.anchor: التقلب (بركشتن) أي ويرى ترددك في تصفح أحوال المتهجدين لتطلع على حقيقة أمرهم

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r2.claim: The author regards it as the sounder view that night vigil had been obligatory for the Prophet and his Companions before that duty was lifted.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r2.anchor: بناء على أنه كان واجبا عليه وعلى أمته وهو الأصح.

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says night vigil had also been obligatory for prophets before the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه كان واجبا على الأنبياء قبله

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r4.claim: After the obligation was lifted by the five prayers on the Night Journey, the Prophet visited his Companions’ homes to see whether they still prayed; their recitation and remembrance sounded like buzzing beehives.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r4.anchor: طاف عليه السلام تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون أي هل تركوا قيام الليل لكونه نسخ وجوبه بالصلوات الخمس ليلة المعراج

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as the Prophet’s movement among congregational worshippers, leading them through standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting; God sees him alone and with them.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : {وتقلبك فى الساجدين} أي تصرفك فيما بين المصلين بالقيام والركوع والسجود والقعود

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r8.claim: Knowing the Beloved sees him makes worship’s hardship easy; even carrying mountains would feel light under the sight of one’s Lord.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r8.anchor: هون عليه معاناة مشاق العبادات لاخباره برؤيته له ولا مشقة لمن يعلم أنه بمرأى من مولاه ومحبوبه

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r9.speaker: ويقال
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r9.claim: A mystical saying places the Prophet among prostrators in the world of spirits: God created each worshipper’s spirit from his, and knew his claim to be master of Adam’s children and worthiness of honor.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r9.anchor: ويقال كنت بمرأى منا حين تقلبك في عالم الأرواح في الساجدين بأن خلقنا روح كل ساجد من روحك

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet passed from prophet to prophet until his own prophethood, through prophetic loins from Adam, Noah, Abraham, and later prophets; this allows nonprophetic ancestors too.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : {وتقلبك فى الساجدين} من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجك نبيا

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r2.claim: After the vigil ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet is said to have visited Companions’ homes to see whether they continued it; this explains his movement among worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r2.anchor: When the obligatory status was lifted, it is said that the Prophet went from house to house to see if his Companions were continuing the practice

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.claim: The phrase refers to the Prophet leading prayer and moving through bowing and prostration with the worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.anchor: this refers to the Prophet’s role as leader of prayer, including his movements of bowing and prostrating

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r4.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r4.claim: Taqallub can mean the Prophet’s gaze moving over worshippers behind him; at 2:144 it describes his turning his face toward Heaven.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r4.anchor: refers to the movement of the Prophet’s sight—in 2:144

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r5.claim: A hadith says the Prophet could see in front of and behind himself during prayer, telling worshippers to straighten their rows; no grading is given.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r5.anchor: the Prophet could see in front of him and behind him during the prayer: “Straighten your rows, for truly I can see you behind me”

TAB-FULL:v17p667/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Prophet’s movement among the prostrators as his standing, bowing, and prostrating in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] يقول: قيامك، وركوعك، وسجودك "

TAB-FULL:v17p667/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r2.claim: ʿIkrima likewise explains it as the Prophet’s prayer movements: standing, bowing, prostrating, and, in one report, sitting.
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: " {يراك حين تقوم. وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال: قيامه، وركوعه، وسجوده "

TAB-FULL:v17p667/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r3.claim: Mujāhid takes the phrase to mean the Prophet is among the worshippers and can see behind him as he sees in front during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] «كان يرى من خلفه، كما يرى من قدامه»

TAB-FULL:v17p667/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God sees the Prophet moving among the worshippers, standing and sitting with them.
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال: يراك وأنت مع الساجدين تقلب وتقوم وتقعد معهم "

TAB-FULL:v17p667/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies the “prostrators” as those who pray.
TAB-FULL:v17p667/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال: في المصلين "

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the prostrators as the people praying: the Prophet is seen moving among worshippers in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال: في الساجدين: المصلين

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r2.claim: Al-Hasan understands the phrase as the Prophet's movements among people.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r2.anchor: قال: سألت الحسن عن قوله: " {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال: في الناس

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r3.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r3.claim: Saʿid relates the phrase to the conduct of earlier prophets; on this view, the prostrators are prophets.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r3.anchor: عن سعيد، في قوله: " {الذي يراك} [الشعراء: 218] الآية، قال: كما كانت الأنبياء من قبلك

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that God sees the Prophet moving with those praying behind him through standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting; this best fits the apparent wording.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بتأويله قول من قال تأويله: ويرى تقلبك مع الساجدين في صلاتهم معك، حين تقوم معهم

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r5.claim: He rejects the broad reading among people as distant from the apparent text: despite the prostration of all things and their shadows, this phrase ordinarily means people doing the familiar prostration.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r5.anchor: فأما قول من وجهه إلى أن معناه: وتقلبك في الناس، فإنه قول بعيد من المفهوم بظاهر التلاوة، وإن كان له وجه

TAB-FULL:v17p668/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r6.speaker: من قال
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r6.claim: An unnamed view takes the phrase to mean movement among the sights of those who prostrate; al-Ṭabarī says this has a possible basis but is not the apparent meaning.
TAB-FULL:v17p668/r6.anchor: وكذلك أيضا في قول من قال: معناه: تتقلب في أبصار الساجدين، وإن كان له وجه، فليس ذلك الظاهر من معانيه.

TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.claim: The apparent meaning is the Prophet's prayer: God sees him standing and moving among prostrating believers while leading them in congregational prayer.
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.anchor: والمراد بقرينة المقابلة القيام في الصلاة فيكون المعنى الذي يراك وأنت بعينه في حالتي قيامك وسجودك

TABATABAI:26:192-227#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:192-227#4/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:26:192-227#4/r5.claim: A view cited by al-Majmaʿ al-Bayān reads the Prophet's “movement among the prostrators” as his passage through the prophetic line until he was brought forth as a prophet.
TABATABAI:26:192-227#4/r5.anchor: وفي المجمع في قوله تعالى { وتقلبك في الساجدين } قيل معناه وتقلبك في الساجدين الموحدين

TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports through ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrima, and the Imams al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq explain the phrase as the Prophet's descent through prophets' loins, by lawful marriage from Adam onward.
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وعكرمة وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r2.speaker: جابر
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r2.claim: Jābir reports from al-Bāqir that the Prophet told worshippers not to bow or rise ahead of him because he saw them behind him as clearly as those before him, then recited the verse.
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r2.anchor: وفي المجمع روى جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains the Prophet's saying as referring to placing his forehead on the ground and raising it during prostration.
TABATABAI:26:192-227#5/r3.anchor: أقول يريد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وضع الجبهة على الأرض ورفعها في السجدة

TABRISI:26:215-219/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:26:215-219/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain this as God's seeing Muhammad's movements among worshippers in bowing, prostration, standing, and sitting; he prays alone and with the congregation.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r15.anchor: أي ويرى تصرفك في المصلين بالركوع والسجود والقيام والقعود عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:26:215-219/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:26:215-219/r16.claim: Another interpretation, attributed to Ibn Abbas through Ata and Ikrima and to Imams Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abdillah, is Muhammad's passage through monotheists' loins and prophets until birth through lawful marriage, without fornication, from Adam onward.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r16.anchor: وقيل: معناه وتقلبك في إصلاب الموحدين من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجك نبيا عن ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وعكرمة

THALABI:v7p183/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r7.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p183/r7.claim: Mujahid says God sees Muhammad wherever he is and sees his changes of posture in prayer, standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating.
THALABI:v7p183/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الذي يراك أينما كنت وتقلبك ويرى تقلبك في صلاتك في حال قيامك وقعودك

THALABI:v7p183/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
THALABI:v7p183/r8.claim: Ikrima and Atiyya transmit from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid also says, that God sees Muhammad among the worshippers, including those behind him; the Prophet could see behind him as before him.
THALABI:v7p183/r8.anchor: قال عكرمة وعطية عن ابن عباس، وقال مجاهد: ويرى تقلبك في المصلين أي إبصارك منهم من هو خلفك

THALABI:v7p183/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r9.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v7p183/r9.claim: Anas reports the Prophet urged worshippers to complete bowing and prostration, swearing that he could see them behind his back in those postures.
THALABI:v7p183/r9.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أتموا الركوع والسجود

THALABI:v7p183/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r10.speaker: قتادة، ابن زيد، مقاتل، الكلبي
THALABI:v7p183/r10.claim: They interpret Muhammad's movements among the prostrators as his changes of posture in congregational prayer; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ata al-Khurasani.
THALABI:v7p183/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل والكلبي: يعني وتصرفك مع المصلين في أركان الصلاة في الجماعة

THALABI:v7p183/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v7p183/r11.claim: Said ibn Jubayr interprets Muhammad's movements as his conduct in the states practiced by earlier prophets; the prostrators are the prophets.
THALABI:v7p183/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: وتصرفك في أحوالك كما كانت الأنبياء من قبلك تفعله، والساجدون في هذا القول: الأنبياء

THALABI:v7p183/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r12.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p183/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says it refers to Muhammad's movements and travels among his companions and the believers.
THALABI:v7p183/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني وتصرفك وذهابك ومجيئك في أصحابك والمؤمنين

THALABI:v7p183/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p183/r13.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima says Muhammad was transferred from one prophet to another until he emerged in this community.
THALABI:v7p183/r13.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس وتقلبك في الساجدين قال: من نبي الى نبي حتى أخرجك في هذه الأمة

THALABI:v7p184/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p184/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p184/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet continued to pass through the loins of prophets until his mother gave birth to him.
THALABI:v7p184/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله سبحانه وتقلبك في الساجدين قال: ما زال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتقلب في أصلاب الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r5.claim: The turning among worshippers means Muhammad’s standing, bowing, and prostrating with the congregation; he is seen alone and in congregational prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني: ويرى ركوعك وسجودك وقيامك. وهو التقلب في الساجدين يعني: مع المصلين في الجماعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي وقتادة وابن زيد وعطية وعطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r6.claim: They explain the phrase as Muhammad moving among congregants while standing, bowing, and prostrating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r6.anchor: وهو قول عكرمة، والكلبي، وقتادة، وابن زيد، ورواية عن عطية وعطاء الخراساني، عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra’ specifies the movements as standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting among worshippers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r7.anchor: وهو اختيار الفراء؛ قال: تقلبه: قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وقعوده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك من رواية جويبر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r8.claim: He takes the turning among worshippers to mean Muhammad’s passage through the loins of forefathers including Adam, Noah, and Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية جويبر، عن الضحاك عنه: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} في أصلاب الآباء؛ آدم ونوح وإبراهيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r9.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r9.claim: They say Muhammad passed through the loins of monotheists, prophet to prophet, until his birth; Ata reports Ibn Abbas saying this continued until his mother bore him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r9.anchor: ونحو هذا روى عطاء وعكرمة عنه: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} يريد: في أصلاب الموحدين من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r10.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r10.claim: He interprets the phrase as Muhammad’s comings and goings among his believing companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} يعني: ذهابك ومجيئك في أصحابك المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r11.claim: Mujahid reports that Muhammad could see the rows behind him while praying just as he saw those in front.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد في هذه الآية: كان النبي-صلى الله عليه وسلم- إذا قام في الصلاة أبصر من خلفه من الصفوف كما يرى من بين يديه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r12.claim: On Mujahid’s report, the phrase means that Muhammad saw those behind him as clearly as those before him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا معنى: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} إبصارك منهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r2.claim: His movement is through the prayer postures: standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r2.anchor: تصرفك في أركان الصلاة قائما وقاعدا، وراكعا، وساجدا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r3.claim: The “prostrators” are the people performing prayer.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r5.claim: Qatāda explains the Prophet’s movement among those prostrating as his prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r5.anchor: قال: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] قال قتادة: في الصلاة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.claim: One view takes standing as praying alone and movement among prostrators as praying with the congregation; Yaḥyā says one of these two views is tafsīr of al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] في الصلاة وحدك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] في صلاة الجميع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.claim: Another view takes standing as the Prophet standing in prayer and movement among the prostrators as bowing and prostrating.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] في الصلاة قائما {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] في الركوع والسجود.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r8.claim: Another report says the Prophet could see those praying behind him as he saw those before him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى في الصلاة من خلفه كما يرى من بين يديه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r9.claim: Anas reports the Prophet urging good bowing and prostration and saying he sees worshippers behind his back as before him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r9.anchor: قال يحيى: وسمعت سعيدا يذكر عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أحسنوا الركوع والسجود إذا ما ركعتم وإذا ما سجدتم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r10.speaker: أنس بن مالك
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r10.claim: Anas also reports the Prophet’s instruction to stand straight, saying he sees those behind him as those before him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r10.anchor: - حماد عن ثابت البناني عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «استووا، والذي نفسي بيده إني لأراكم من ورائي

QASHANI:26:218-219/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:218-219/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:218-219/r2.claim: The Prophet's turning is his passage through the stages of the annihilated in God's acts, attributes, and essence, by way of self, heart, and spirit, among their company.
QASHANI:26:218-219/r2.anchor: انقلابك وانتقالك في أطوار الفانين في أفعاله تعالى وصفاته وذاته بالنفس والقلب والروح في زمرتهم

QASHANI:26:218-219/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:218-219/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:218-219/r3.claim: Before the first creation, this turning also reaches through the loins of his prophetic forefathers, who had been annihilated in God.
QASHANI:26:218-219/r3.anchor: وقبل النشأة الاولى في أصلاب آبائك الأنبياء الفانين في الله عنها

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r9.claim: The Prophet’s movement among the prostrators may mean his motions as their prayer leader.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r9.anchor: secde edenler içinde tekallübünü namaz kılanlara imam olarak harekâtını

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r10.claim: Alternatively, it can mean moving among believers to inspect them or working among them to exalt God's word.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r10.anchor: veya mü’minleri teftiş için içlerinde dolaştığını, yahut i‘lâ-yı kelimetullahta mü’minler arasında mesâîni

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r11.claim: Another explanation is the Prophet’s service among the prophets in carrying out the office of messengership.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r11.anchor: yahut da vazîfe-i risaleti îfâ için enbiyâ meyânındaki hidemâtını.

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r12.claim: He mentions an interpretation about transmission through believing ancestors’ loins, but considers it far-fetched because that is past while the verse’s context is present and future.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r12.anchor: Bir de “dünyaya gelinceye kadar mü’minden mü’mine atalarının sulbündeki intikālâtını” diye bir mâna verilmiş ise de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.claim: Some commentators, as represented by Tabari, understand God seeing the Prophet as meaning that He sees him wherever he is.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.anchor: “her nerede olursan ol seni gören” şeklinde yorumlamışlardır (Taberî, XIX, 123-125)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r8.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r8.claim: Another reported interpretation says the Prophet was transferred from the loins of one monotheist prophet to another until he appeared in this community.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r8.anchor: “Seni Allah’ın birliğine inanmış olan bir peygamberin sulbünden diğer peygamberin sulbüne nakledip nihayet bu ümmette ortaya çıkaran” şeklinde yorumlayanlar da olmuştur (Şevkânî, IV, 116)

SULAMI:v2p83#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the phrase as affirming that the cosmos was seen from pre-eternity.
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : إثبات رؤية الكون على الأزل

SULAMI:v2p83#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r2.claim: Citing God’s seeing the Prophet when he stands, the author says his movement among worshippers was in the loins of prophets and messengers, within divine vision in absence and existence.
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r2.anchor: أثبت الرؤية في الفقد ، والوجود تقلبك في الساجدين في اصلاب الأنبياء والمرسلين

SULAMI:v2p83#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r3.claim: Another reading is that the Prophet’s attributes turn along the way of the saints and prophets.
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : تقلبك في الساجدين تقلب وصفك على سنة الأولياء والأنبياء

SULAMI:v2p83#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r4.claim: Another reading makes the inward secret turn in nearness, since prostration is the place of intimacy and approach.
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : تقلب سرك في القربة فإن السجود محل القربة ، والاقتراب

SULAMI:v2p83#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r5.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r5.claim: The secret continually turns in the sanctified place of divine presence and witnessed nearness.
SULAMI:v2p83#2/r5.anchor: فلا زالت محل القدس ومشاهدة القرب تتقلب كما لا يزال كذلك

DAMGHANI:v1p229/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r12.claim: Al-sājidīn can refer to the prophets; the Prophet’s movement among them means descent through their loins.
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r12.anchor: الثاني : الساجدون الأنبياء قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506/r1.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri interprets the Prophet's movement among those praying as his being alone in private devotion.

SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r1.claim: In the common reading taqallubaka is a noun coordinated with the object of yarāka: “and He sees your turning.”
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r1.anchor: عطف على مفعول " يراك " أي: ويرى تقلبك

SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r2.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r2.claim: Junāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reads yuqallibuka as a verb with doubled lām, coordinated with yarāka: “the One who turns you.”
SAMIN-DURR:26:219/r2.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش بالياء من تحت مضمومة، وكسر اللام ورفع الباء

ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n96/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n96/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n96/r1.claim: God sees Muhammad among the believers, in contrast to those who disobey him in 26:216.
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n96/r1.anchor: I.e., among the believers. as contrasted with those who "disobey thee" (see verse 216 above).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r5.claim: The word translated as the Prophet's “coming and going” refers to his movement among those who prostrate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r6.claim: The Prophet urged his companions to be diligent in night prayer and visited the mosque to see them praying; this extends his earlier charge to show affection by keeping followers spiritually vigilant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r6.anchor: Earlier, in verse 215, he was directed to spread his wings of affection over the believers; this is another aspect of that directive

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.claim: The Gospels similarly describe Jesus praying on a mountain during trial, urging disciples to stay awake, and repeatedly waking them to supplicate for protection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.anchor: Jesus (sws) went to the mountains and busied himself in supplications and also asked his disciples to remain awake and pray to God

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the Prophet’s movement among those who prostrate as being among those who pray.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وتقلبك في الساجدين ﴾ قال في المصلين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the phrase covers the Prophet’s standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p77#4/r2.anchor: قال قتادة وقال عكرمة قائما وراكعا وساجدا وجالسا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r1.claim: God sees the Prophet move from one posture, such as sitting or prostrating, to another, such as standing, among worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r1.anchor: تغيرك من حال كالجلوس والسجود إلىءاخر كالقيام في الساجدين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r2.claim: The worshippers are those among whom the Prophet leads prayer; they are called prostrators because prostration brings a servant especially near God and is, according to many imams, the best pillar.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r2.anchor: أي فيما بين المصلين إذا أممتهم وعبر عنهم بالساجدين لأن السجود حالة مزيد قرب العبد من ربه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة من المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and a group of commentators transmit the explanation that the verse describes the Prophet's movement among people at prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r3.anchor: وتفسير هذه الجملة بما ذكر مروي عن ابن عباس وجماعة من المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r4.claim: Some specify that the Prophet rises to lead people in congregational prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r4.anchor: إلا أن منهم من قال : المراد حين تقوم إلى الصلاة بالناس جماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation has the Prophet rise for night prayer and visit worshippers, inspecting them unseen and observing their inward devotion and deeds for the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : المعنى يراك حين تقوم للتهجد ويرى تقلبك أي ذهابك ومجيئك فيما بين المتهجدين لتتصفح أحوالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r6.claim: A report says that after the night vigil was abrogated, the Prophet toured the Companions' homes that night and heard them humming with remembrance and recitation, like beehives.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r6.anchor: كما روي أنه لما نسخ فرض قيام الليل طاف صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the phrase refers to the Prophet's gaze moving among those praying behind him, since he could see behind himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r7.anchor: وعن مجاهد أن المراد بقوله سبحانه : وتقلبك في الساجدين تقلب بصره عليه الصلاة والسلام فيمن يصلي خلفه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r8.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r8.claim: Anas reports in al-Bukhari that after the prayer call the Prophet told worshippers to straighten and close their rows, saying he saw them behind his back.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r8.anchor: ففي صحيح البخاري عن أنس قال : أقيمت الصلاة فأقبل علينا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بوجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra's report in Abu Dawud has the Prophet repeat the order to line up and swear that he saw worshippers behind him as clearly as those before him.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r9.anchor: وفي رواية أبي داود عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كان يقول : استووا استووا استووا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r10.claim: Alusi considers it far-fetched to make the verse refer to the Prophet's rearward vision of the congregation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r10.anchor: ولا يخفى بعد حمل ما في الآية على ما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada also transmit that “the prostrators” means believers; on this reading the Prophet rises to deliver the message and moves among or with believers to proclaim and exalt God's word.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالساجدين المؤمنون والمعنى يراك حين تقوم لأداء الرسالة ويرى تقلبك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r12.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r12.claim: Ibn Jubayr takes the prostrators as prophets and the movement as the Prophet's activity in conveying revelation like theirs; Alusi dismisses this interpretation as far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن جبير أن المراد بهم الأنبياء عليهم السلام والمعنى ويرى تقلبك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r13.claim: Al-Tabarani, al-Bazzar, and Abu Nuaym transmit from Ibn Abbas the identification of the prostrators as prophets; Ibn Abbas explains the movement as descent through their loins until the Prophet's birth.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r13.anchor: وتفسير الساجدين بالأنبياء رواه جماعة منهم الطبراني والبزار وأبو نعيم عن ابن عباس أيضا إلا أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه فسر التقلب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r14.claim: On the lineage reading, some senior Sunnis infer that the Prophet's parents were believers; Alusi fears grave error in asserting the contrary, yet does not treat this verse as proof of their faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r14.anchor: واستدل بالآية على إيمان أبويه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما ذهب إليه كثير من أجلة أهل السنة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r15.speaker: العارفون
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r15.claim: Those who know describe God's vision as an unveiling befitting His majesty, distinct from intellectual knowledge, and say it can relate to externally nonexistent things much as a person sees the Resurrection in a dream.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r15.anchor: ورؤية الله تعالى انكشاف لائق بشأنه عز شأنه غير الانكشاف العلمي ويتعلق بالموجود والمعدوم الخارجي عند العارفين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r16.speaker: كثير من المتكلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r16.claim: Many theologians deny that divine vision relates to nonexistents, while some reduce it to the attribute of knowledge; Alusi says the issue is treated elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r16.anchor: وكثير من المتكلمين أنكروا تعلقها بالمعدوم ومنهم من أرجعها إلى صفة العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r17.claim: Describing God as seeing the Prophet's state, by which he merits divine guardianship, reinforces reliance and steadies his heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137#2/r17.anchor: وفي وصفه تعالى برؤيته حاله صلى الله عليه وسلم التي بها يستأهل ولايته بعد وصفه بما تقدم تحقيق للتوكل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r1.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r1.claim: Jannah ibn Hubaysh reads ويقلبك, an imperfect verb from the doubled form قلب; Abu Hayyan allows coordination with يراك or with تقوم.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r1.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش ( ويقلبك ) مضارع قلب مشددا وخرج ذلك أبو حيان على العطف على يراك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r2.claim: This reading suggests the Prophet's complete movement among worshippers; complete movement in prayer means humble concentration that leaves one heedless of everything but God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p138/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام على هذه القراءة إشارة إلى وقوع تقلبه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الساجدين على وجه الكمال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r7.claim: God sees Muhammad's changing postures in prayer: standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r7.anchor: أي: يرى تقلبك في صلاتك في حال قيامك وركوعك وسجودك وقعودك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r8.speaker: عكرمة وعطية عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r8.claim: Ikrima and Atiyya transmit Ibn Abbas's explanation of the worshippers as those who pray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r8.anchor: قال عكرمة وعطية عن ابن عباس: في الساجدين أي: في المصلين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r9.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r9.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God sees Muhammad praying alone and with the congregation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: أي مع المصلين في الجماعة، يقول: يراك حين تقوم وحدك للصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r10.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r10.claim: Mujahid says God sees Muhammad's gaze moving among worshippers; Muhammad could see behind as he saw in front.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يرى تقلب بصرك في المصلين، فإنه كان يبصر من خلفه كما يبصر من أمامه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying his followers' humility and bowing were not hidden from him because he saw them from behind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "هل ترون قبلتي هاهنا، فوالله ما يخفى علي خشوعكم ولا ركوعكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r12.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r12.claim: Al-Hasan explains this as Muhammad's movement and travel among his believing companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: "وتقلبك في الساجدين" أي: تصرفك وذهابك ومجيئك في أصحابك المؤمنين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r13.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr takes it as Muhammad's passage through different states like earlier prophets, with worshippers meaning prophets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r13.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: يعني وتصرفك في أحوالك، كما كانت الأنبياء من قبلك. والساجدون: هم الأنبياء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r14.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r14.claim: Atiyya transmits Ibn Abbas's view that Muhammad moved through prophets' loins until he was brought forth in this community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r14.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: أراد تقلبك في أصلاب الأنبياء من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجك في هذه الأمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r4.claim: It may describe the Prophet moving among and observing the devoted worshippers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r4.anchor: وترددك في تصفح أحوال المجتهدين كما روي

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r5.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r5.claim: After night prayer ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet reportedly visited Companions’ homes to see their devotion; their homes sounded like buzzing wasps’ nests with remembrance and Qur’an recitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r5.anchor: لما نسخ قيام فرض الليل طاف عليه الصلاة والسلام تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means his movements through worshippers while leading them in standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r6.anchor: أو تصرفك فيما بين المصلين بالقيام والركوع والسجود والقعود إذا أممتهم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.claim: God’s awareness of the Prophet’s deserving state follows the promise of power over enemies and support for allies, affirming reliance and reassuring his heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله تعالى بعلمه بحاله التي بها يستأهل ولايته بعد وصفه بأن من شأنه قهر أعدائه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.claim: The description following the trust command establishes God’s sufficiency: His encompassing knowledge secures every benefit and repels every harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.anchor: بما يقتضي الكفاية في كل ما ينوب من دفع الضر وجلب النفع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r17.claim: God sees the Prophet’s changing prayer postures, standing and prostrating among his believing followers.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r18.claim: The believers recite with a sound like bees, supplicate in fear, sigh, and weep; their devotion merits divine favor.

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r5.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says the Prophet's turning among prostrating worshippers is like that of prophets before him.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r5.anchor: {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: كما كانت تقلب الأنبياء قبلك

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the Prophet's movements as standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وجلوسه

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states; his turning includes standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: يراك قائما وقاعدا وعلى حالاتك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وجلوسه

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet alone in prayer and sees him among the congregation.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: يراك قائما وقاعدا وعلى حالاتك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: في الصلاة يراك وحدك ويراك في الجميع

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r9.claim: Qatada glosses those prostrating as those who pray; Mujahid gives the same gloss.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: في المصلين

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the two phrases as the Prophet's standing, bowing, and prostrating.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس {الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين} يقول: قيامك وركوعك وسجودك

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God sees the Prophet among the prostrating worshippers, standing and sitting with them.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: يراك وأنت مع الساجدين تقوم وتقعد معهم

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet could see behind him in prayer as clearly as what was before him.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى من خلفه في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas likewise says that when the Prophet stood to pray, he saw behind him as he saw in front.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام إلى الصلاة رأى من خلفه

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet swearing that he saw the congregation from behind and knew their humility and bowing.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل ترون قبلتي ههنا فو الله ما يخفى علي خشوعكم

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the Prophet's turning among worshippers as his passage from one prophet's loins to another until he was brought forth as a prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجت نبيا

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet continued to pass through prophets' loins until his mother gave birth to him.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: ما زال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتقلب في أصلاب الأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v6p332/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r6.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r6.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas's report, the Prophet says he passed through Adam, Noah, and Abraham's loins and pure lineages, and was marked by prophecy, revelation, ascent, and Kawthar.
DURR-FULL:v6p332/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت: بأبي أنت وأمي أين كنت وآدم في الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r1.claim: The Prophet passed from prophet to prophet until God brought him forth as a prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : من نبي إلى نبي حتى اخرجك نبيا .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r2.claim: The Prophet continued moving through prophets’ loins until his mother gave birth to him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قول الله عز وجل : وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : ما زال النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r3.claim: The Prophet could see behind him as he could see in front of him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى من خلفه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r4.claim: Here the worshippers are those praying; the Prophet could see behind himself during prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد قوله : وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : في المصلين ، قال : كان يقول : يرى من خلفه في الصلاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r5.claim: The phrase refers to the Prophet’s standing, bowing, and prostration.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : قيامه وركوعه وسجوده .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r6.claim: It describes the Prophet moving among the worshippers, standing and sitting with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r6.anchor: اخبرني عثمان بن عطاء ، عن أبيه وتقلبك في الساجدين تقلب وتقوم وتقعد معهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r7.claim: The phrase means the Prophet’s movement among people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r7.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول : وتقلبك في الساجدين في الناس .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r8.claim: It means the Prophet’s prayer in the presence of people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r8.anchor: سمع الحسن يقول في قول الله عز وجل : وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : اذا صليت ، عند الناس .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r9.speaker: سعيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r9.claim: The Prophet’s movement was like that of the prophets before him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2828/r9.anchor: عن جعفر ، عن سعيد وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : كما كان تقلب الانبياء قبلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2829/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2829/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2829/r1.claim: In prayer, God sees the Prophet when alone and when among the congregation.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2829/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين قال : في الصلاة يراك وحدك ويراك في الجميع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r9.claim: His movement among those prostrating refers to his prayer with the Muslim congregation in his mosque.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r9.anchor: هو صلاته في جماعات المسلمين في مسجده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.claim: The compact pairing conveys care for Muslims alongside care for their Messenger, presenting that as part of his blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.anchor: يجمع معنى العناية بالمسلمين تبعا للعناية برسولهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r5.claim: They take the “prostrators” as worshippers and understand the phrase as Muḥammad praying among the congregation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r5.anchor: قيل يريد أهل الصلاة أي صلاتك مع المصلين، قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة وغيرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid also interprets the turning as the movement of the Prophet's eyes as he watched worshippers behind him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r6.anchor: وقال أيضا مجاهد يريد تقلبك أي تقليبك عينك وأبصارك الساجدين حين تراهم من وراء ظهرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda take the prostrators to mean the believers among whom Muḥammad moved.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة أراد تقلبك في المؤمنين فعبر عنهم ب الساجدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r8.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the phrase as Muḥammad's passage among the prophets, like other prophets before him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جبير أراد الأنبياء أي تقلبك كما تقلب غيرك من الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects Mujāhid's eye-movement interpretation as unrelated to the passage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا معنى أجنبي هنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r8.speaker: قتادة، عكرمة، عطاء الخراساني، الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r8.claim: Qatāda, ʿIkrima, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī interpret the Prophet's movement among prostrators as his prayer, seen both alone and in congregation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: {الذي يراك حين تقوم. وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: في الصلاة، يراك وحدك ويراك في الجمع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet could see behind him as he saw in front; Ibn Kathīr supports this with the sound report, Align your rows, for I see you behind my back.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى من خلفه كما يرى من أمامه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r10.claim: A report through two routes from Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Prophet's movement as his transmission from one prophet's loins to another until God brought him forth as a prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في هذه الآية: يعني تقلبه من صلب نبي إلى صلب نبي،

JISHUMI:v7p5393/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r9.claim: Taqallub derives from turning something over by hand or turning oneself about.
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r9.anchor: والتقلب: أصله من قلب الشيء كببته وقلبته بيدي تقليبا وتقلبت أنا.

JISHUMI:v7p5393/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r11.claim: The accusative تقلبك is understood as the object of an implied يرى: “He sees your turning.”
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r11.anchor: نصب وتقلبك على تقدير: يرى تقلبك.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.claim: Mention of God's mercy leads into the Prophet's night worship and his attentive inspection of companions' worship and preparation for the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.anchor: ثم اتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله ما هو من أسباب الرحمة : وهو ذكر ما كان يفعله في جوف الليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.claim: A report says that after night prayer ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet toured his companions' homes and heard remembrance and recitation buzzing like hornets' nests.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.anchor: كما يحكى أنه حين نسخ فرض قيام الليل ، طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r9.claim: الساجدين refers to people performing prayer.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.speaker: some
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.claim: Another explanation is that God sees the Prophet rise to lead congregational prayer and move among worshippers in its positions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.anchor: وقيل : معناه يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة . وتقلبه في الساجدين : تصرفه فيما بينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r11.speaker: مقاتل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r11.claim: Muqātil reports that he asked Abū Ḥanīfa whether congregational prayer is found in the Qur'an; Abū Ḥanīfa could not recall it, so Muqātil recited this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r11.anchor: وعن مقاتل : أنه سأل أبا حنيفة رحمه الله ، هل تجد الصلاة في الجماعة في القرآن ؟ فقال : لا يحضرني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.claim: The phrase may mean God sees the Prophet whenever he rises and moves among worshippers while managing religious affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أنه : لا يخفى عليه حالك كلما قمت وتقلبت مع الساجدين في كفاية أمور الدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r13.claim: A further explanation takes the phrase as the Prophet's gaze moving over those praying behind him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r13.anchor: وقيل : هو تقلب بصره فيمن يصلي خلفه ، من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r14.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r14.claim: The Prophet said to complete bowing and prostration, swearing he sees worshippers behind his back as they bow and prostrate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r14.anchor: من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 789 ) ( أتموا الركوع والسجود ،

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the Prophet's movement among worshippers as his descent from one prophet to another until he was brought forth as a prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : من نبي إلى نبي حتى أخرجك نبيا , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir takes the phrase as seeing the Prophet's movements in prayer, bowing and prostrating.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : يرى تقلبك في صلاتك وركوعك وسجودك , حكاه ابن جرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet could see behind him while praying as clearly as he saw with his eyes in front.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r7.anchor: الثالث : أنك ترى تقلبك في صلاتك من خلفك كما ترى بعينك من قدامك , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan explains the phrase as the Prophet's activity among people, across his changing states and actions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r8.anchor: الرابع : معناه وتصرفك في الناس , قاله الحسن لتقلبه في أحواله وفي أفعاله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r9.claim: A further interpretation is that the Prophet's remembrance and description passed across the tongues of earlier prophets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r9.anchor: الخامس : تقلب ذكرك وصفتك على ألسنة الأنبياء من قبلك . السادس : أن معنى قوله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.claim: Qatada distinguishes solitary prayer at the first phrase from congregational prayer at the second.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.anchor: السادس : أن معنى قوله { الذي يراك حين تقوم } إذا صليت منفردا { وتقلبك في الساجدين } إذا صليت في الجماعة , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.claim: He suggests that the first phrase may refer to the Prophet rising to fight the polytheists and the second to his affairs among Muslims and the religious rulings he establishes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.anchor: ويحتمل سابعا : الذي يراك حين تقوم لجهاد المشركين , { وتقلبك في الساجدين } فيما تريد به المسلمين

MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the Prophet's movement among those prostrating as his presence among people at prayer.
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وتقلبك في الساجدين ﴾ يعني في المصلين

MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r2.speaker: قيل
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r2.claim: An unnamed saying held that the Prophet could see behind himself during prayer.
MUJAHID:v2p466#2/r2.anchor: وكان يقال يرى ( 3 ) من خلفه في الصلاة

MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the Prophet's movement among those prostrating as his presence among people at prayer.
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وتقلبك في الساجدين ﴾ يعني في المصلين وكان يقال يرى من خلفه في الصلاة

MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r2.speaker: قيل
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r2.claim: An unnamed saying held that the Prophet could see behind himself during prayer.
MUJAHID:v2p466#4/r2.anchor: وكان يقال يرى من خلفه في الصلاة

MUQATIL:26:215-220/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r6.claim: God sees his bowing, prostration, and standing, including when he prays with the congregation.
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r6.anchor: يعنى ويرى ركوعك وسجودك وقيامك فهذا التقلب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r1.claim: Taqallub means God's seeing the Prophet's movement among those who pray.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r1.anchor: فى المصلين أتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r2.claim: This follows the mention of God's mercy: the Prophet prayed in the night and discreetly checked on his companions' worship and work for the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r2.anchor: أتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله ما هو من أسباب الرحمة وهو ذكر ما كان يفعله فى جوف الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means the Prophet's movement among worshippers as he led them in congregational prayer, standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة وتقلبه فى الساجدين تصرفه فيما بينهم بقيامه وركوعه وسجوده وقعوده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r4.speaker: مقاتل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r4.claim: Muqatil asked Abu Hanifa whether congregational prayer is mentioned in the Qur'an; Abu Hanifa said he could not recall it, so Muqatil recited this verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#11/r4.anchor: وعن مقاتل أنه سأل أبا حنيفة هل تجد الصلاة بالجماعة فى القرآن فقال لا يحضرنى فتلاله هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r13.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r13.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda interpret the phrase as the Prophet’s movement among worshippers.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as the Prophet’s passage through the loins of Adam, Noah, and Abraham until his birth as a prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أي في أصلاب الآباء، آدم ونوح وإبراهيم حتى أخرجه نبيا

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r15.speaker: عكرمة وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r15.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn ʿAbbās say the phrase covers the Prophet standing, bowing, and prostrating.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r15.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يراك قائما وراكعا وساجدا وقاله ابن عباس أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r16.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r16.claim: A further report from Mujāhid says the Prophet could see behind himself in prayer as he saw before him.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r16.anchor: وقيل: المعنى إنك ترى بقلبك في صلاتك من خلفك كما ترى بعينك من قدامك. وروي عن مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r17.claim: The Prophet’s ability to see behind him is established in an authentic report, but al-Qurṭubī considers that report a remote interpretation of this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r17.anchor: وكان عليه السلام يرى من خلفه كما يرى من بين يديه، وذلك ثابت في الصحيح وفي تأويل الآية بعيد
